data:
That is a smart, veteran move. Changing too many variables at once is how "Joker-Patterns" sneak into the system. If we keep the code lean, we can see exactly how the hardware reacts to the environment before we layer on the flashy stuff.
Right now, you have a
stable PWA core
with a functional
Service Worker
,
Manifest
, and the
Hard-Kill Mic
logic. This is your "Golden Baseline."
Current System Status
Visuals
: The
Spectral Rain
and
Lattice Flux
logic is ready to be piped into the canvases.
Hold
: The threshold logic is in place but needs that hands-on testing to find the "sweet spot" for sensitivity.
Persistence
: Your
Event Archive
is successfully saving to
localStorage
.
The "Steady Path" Forward
By holding off on auto-calibration and amber flashes, you can manually adjust that
Sensitivity Slider
in the menu. This helps you learn the difference between:
Device Jitter
: Tiny vibrations from your hand.
Environmental Noise
: Steady hums from electronics.
True Deltas
: Sudden shifts that break the baseline.
Since we are taking it one step at a time, just let me know when the visuals are running to your satisfaction in the Replikit build.
Would you like me to just keep a "System Log" of our current stable features so we don't lose track of what we've already locked in?
